extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, law students, and judges studying U.S. patent assignment, title, and license doctrine
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes legal rules governing patent assignments, equitable title, grants, mortgages, tenancy, death, bankruptcy, creditor proceedings, and licenses under U.S. law as presented in a legal treatise chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied present transfer of title in assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Title is implied in every assignment of a patent right unless the assignment purports to convey merely the right of the assignor or is otherwise limited to narrower ground than the entire patent right which it describes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignment that purports to convey the entire patent right transfers whatever title the assignor may subsequently acquire by purchase or otherwise; but an assignment of the right, title, and interest 'without anything more' will not operate to convey any title subsequently acquired by the assignor.

rubrics_metrics.name: No implied warranty of validity in assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: No warranty of validity is implied in any assignment of a patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignor knows the patent to be invalid when making the assignment, that constitutes fraud and the assignee may seek relief on that ground; but where both parties are innocent of knowledge of invalidity, the loss falls on the then owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of invalid patent is sufficient consideration (absent warranty/fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment of an invalid patent is a sufficient consideration to support a promissory note where there is neither warranty nor fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing an assignee who profited from the patent to defend nonpayment by later alleging invalidity would be unjust; courts reject a failure-of-consideration theory that would let assignees avoid promised payments for assigned patents in such circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express warranties of validity may be incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: Express warranties of validity can be incorporated into patent assignments and, when so incorporated, will subject assignors to actions for damages if the patents assigned are in fact invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parol warranties accompanying written assignments are inadmissible as foundations for damages actions based solely on alleged invalidity, but such parol statements may be admissible as evidence of fraud where other evidence shows the assignor knew the patent was invalid at the time of assignment; in such a case the action rests on fraud, not the parol warranty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable title accrues on grant to inventor or assignee chargeable with notice
rubrics_metrics.description: An equitable title accrues to an assignee when a patent is granted to an inventor, or to a subsequent assignee chargeable with notice, for an invention made, completed, or patented after execution of an assignment adapted to convey it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document that purports to convey a patent and all improvements that may thereafter be made by the assignor is an example of an assignment producing equitable title to subsequent improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements included when instrument purports to convey them
rubrics_metrics.description: A document which conveys a patent and purports also to convey all improvements on the invention which may thereafter be made by the assignor transfers those improvements (equitable title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'improvement' may be an addition increasing value or a substitute that supplants the original by performing its function more efficiently or cheaply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable title to inventor where assignment includes covenant to pay proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: An equitable title accrues to an inventor when a patent is granted to his assignee pursuant to an assignment accompanied by a contract providing that the assignee should pay the inventor all or some portion of the proceeds of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, equitable titles may accrue to assignees of a term for years limited to expire before patent expiration, to consolidated corporations, or to employers under specific contract-to-invent arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer acquisition of title from employee invention (specific-purpose rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer acquires title where an employee makes an invention in pursuance of a contract to invent for that employer, but the employment must be specifically for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a contract may be oral and not within the statute of frauds; courts look to whether the employment was specifically for inventing for employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable interests from contracts or constructive trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract purporting to give a person a beneficial interest in a patent, though not amounting to an assignment or license, can create an equitable title; facts that would create a constructive or resulting trust in other intangible property will have the same effect for patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable titles may therefore arise without formal assignment if the circumstances merit a trust or beneficial interest recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable title to unspecified beneficiaries (trustee assignments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is assigned to a specified person as trustee without stating the character of the trust or the identity of beneficiaries, an equitable title may arise to unspecified persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the nature of the trust and the beneficiaries can be established by parol evidence, and the equitable title may be enforced against the trustee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of equitable title into legal title by equity
rubrics_metrics.description: An equitable title to a patent right may be translated into a legal title by specific performance of contract or other action in equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity may also enforce equitable title against holders of the naked legal title where no affirmative relief is sought by the equitable title holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: bona fide purchaser without notice defeats prior equitable interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the holder of the legal title assigns the patent to a purchaser for a valuable consideration without notice of a prior equitable title, such purchaser takes the entire ownership freed from the prior equitable encumbrance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Between equal equities the law will generally prevail; caveat emptor applies only where seller has no title at all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants are territorial and not divisible except territorially
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant conveys the entire right or an undivided interest within a specified portion of the territory of the United States; the title to the subject matter of letters patent is not divisible in any other category than a territorial one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore grants cannot be made to convey one of several inventions covered by a patent, nor to convey an exclusive right to make/use/sell for only one of several purposes to which the invention is applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and effect of grants (ambiguity, forfeiture, licenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant is not void for territorial ambiguity where reservations are capable of becoming certain by competent evidence; clauses of forfeiture or obligations to prosecute suits are not inconsistent with a grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grant is not forfeited by failure to pay royalty or keep other promises unless the grant expressly provides such a forfeiture; a grant may be subject to an outstanding license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot reserve conflicting partial rights in a grant
rubrics_metrics.description: No instrument can be a grant which reserves to the grantor a right to make but not to sell or use, or to sell but not to make or use, specimens of the patented thing within the territory covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserving only fragmentary substantive rights to the grantor (e.g., make without sell/use) is inconsistent with a proper grant of the exclusive right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusive territorial grant: resale/use outside territory
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant of an exclusive right to make, use, and sell a patented invention within a particular part of the United States confers the right to use and sell anywhere within the United States those specimens which are made and sold under the grant and within the territory covered thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus specimens lawfully made and sold under the grant within the grantee's territory may be used and sold elsewhere in the United States by the grantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements between owners as to territorial non-use not binding on purchasers
rubrics_metrics.description: An agreement between owners not to permit any sale or use of the subject of their patent in the territory of each other is not binding upon purchasers of the patented articles from either owner, even where purchasers knew of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such owner-owner understandings do not bind downstream purchasers as to their right to buy/sell the articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign sales do not exhaust U.S. patent rights (no U.S. exhaustion by foreign sale)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawful sale in a foreign country of an article patented there and also in the United States does not authorize use or sale in the United States of the article sold abroad, even if the maker/seller abroad had the right from the U.S. patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patentee owning both U.S. and foreign patents may lawfully couple foreign sales with a restriction prohibiting importation into the United States; that restriction will bind persons in the U.S. who have knowledge or notice of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgages of patent rights and effects of Patent Office recording
rubrics_metrics.description: A mortgage may cover the entire patent or an undivided part, or rights within a specified part of the U.S.; due recording of such a mortgage in the Patent Office makes the mortgagee's title complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recorded mortgagee is entitled to grant licenses, receive royalties, bring suits against infringers, and recover profits or damages while the mortgage remains in force; the mortgage continues until debt payment or redemption; it will not affect an outstanding license, especially where the mortgagee had notice of that license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor's bill effects and jurisdictional note
rubrics_metrics.description: A creditor's bill may transfer complete or equitable title to a patent whenever a judgment is obtained and execution is returned nulla bona; the court may appoint a trustee or master to execute a proper assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A creditor's bill is not a patent suit that confers federal jurisdiction; where federal jurisdiction is lacking, proceedings must be in state court or by supplementary execution procedures under state codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bankruptcy vests trustee with bankrupt's patent title (limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Bankruptcy Act of 1898, adjudication of bankruptcy vests in the trustee whatever title the bankrupt had in any patent or patent right or right of action thereunder at the date of adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rights so acquired include estoppels that favored the bankrupt; however, a pending application is not a 'patent right' or 'property' within certain statutory clauses and so does not pass to the trustee.

rubrics_metrics.name: State insolvency and dissolved corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: State insolvency proceedings generally do not confer a legal title to patents on an assignee in insolvency, though a state court may compel assignment to reach patents for debt payment; patents of dissolved corporations usually pass under state law to receivers or officials winding up affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mechanics and effects differ from federal bankruptcy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer on death: inchoate and existing titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Death of an inventor before grant transfers his inchoate title to his executor or administrator in trust for heirs or devisees; death of an owner of any legal or equitable title causes transfer of that title to his executor or administrator in the same manner as other intangible personal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executor/administrator may convey by written assignment or grant with proper probate authority; an assignment by one of several joint representatives is effective for all; misnomer of executor/administrator does not invalidate conveyance; if executor takes no action and is discharged, ownership devolves on heirs-at-law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenancy in common in patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenancy in common arises when the sole owner conveys an undivided interest, or when joint inventors obtain a joint patent or multiple persons obtain undivided ownership by one assignment; ordinary incidents of tenancy in common apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each co-tenant is entitled to use the invention without accounting to others; each may make, use, sell, and license without consent of co-tenants, and neither co-tenant nor his licensees can be enjoined by another co-tenant or made to account for profits in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of action for third-party infringement belongs to all co-owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent held by tenants in common has been infringed by a third party, the right of action for that infringement belongs in common to all the owners and cannot be fully released by either of them alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual co-owners cannot unilaterally release the common right of action in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on trustee-only sales when trust prohibits partial conveyance
rubrics_metrics.description: An agreement by a trustee of a patent (who is himself one of the beneficiaries) to sell the patent cannot be specifically enforced as to the trustee's own interest where the trust's object was to prevent less than all joint owners from conveying or granting licenses, and where the vendee had notice of the trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity will refuse specific enforcement that would defeat the trust's essential purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition and removal of clouds on patent title
rubrics_metrics.description: Partition of a patent right held in tenancy in common can be made by common consent of all owners but not against the will of any owner; equity has jurisdiction to remove a cloud on title consisting of an express or implied assertion of adverse ownership or encumbrance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable relief is available to clear title disputes among co-owners or adverse claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of license (distinguished from assignment/grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any conveyance of a right under a patent which does not amount to an assignment or to a grant is a license; a license may be granted at any time after the application for patent is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A conveyance is a license (not an assignment) if it does not convey the entire and unqualified monopoly or an undivided interest therein throughout the territory to which it refers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive rights separable: make, use, sell
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to manufacture, the right to sell, and the right to use are each substantive rights and may be granted or conferred separately by the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include exclusive rights to make and sell but not to use; make and use but not to sell; or use and sell but not to make; courts accept these as licenses rather than assignments where territory/interest is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied rights necessary for enjoyment of expressed license
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of express reservation, some licenses are extended by implication to convey rights necessary to the full enjoyment of the rights expressly conveyed (maxim: one granting a thing implicitly grants that without which the thing expressly granted would be useless).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a matter of construing the language actually written (not parol enlargement) and depends on the circumstances surrounding the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express license to make implies use or sell depending on circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: An express license to make specimens of a patented thing is without value unless it implies a right to use or to sell the specimens made; whether use or sale is implied depends on surrounding circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the licensee was engaged in a business making it convenient to use the thing, the right to use will be implied in preference to a right to sell; if the licensee had no occasion to use the thing, right to sell may be the natural implication.
